OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 8, 2026 (11:03 a.m. EST audit)

STATUS: Direct time-stamped Diversion Canal discharge, direction and current velocity NOT independently verified. Santee Cooper's operator feed says updated November 8; its most recent DAILY lake elevations are dated November 7 (not November 8), without individual observation times. Do not interpret facility generation or tentative schedules as measured canal flow.

OPERATOR-PUBLISHED DAILY ELEVATIONS (feet; measurement times unspecified): November 7: Lake Marion 74.25, Lake Moultrie 74.18, nominal difference 0.07 ft (Marion higher). November 6: Marion 74.26, Moultrie 74.17, difference 0.09 ft. November 5: Marion 74.24, Moultrie 74.13, difference 0.11 ft. From November 6 to November 7 Marion fell 0.01 ft and Moultrie rose 0.01 ft; the nominal difference narrowed 0.02 ft, from 0.09 to 0.07 ft. Operator daily elevations are not individually time-stamped; USGS station data/datum pages returned HTTP 403 during this audit, so independent synchronization and datum reconciliation could not be performed. The differences are provisional and NOT verified simultaneous hydraulic head measurements.

HYDRO SCHEDULE (operator feed updated November 8; tentative, subject to change): Sunday November 8 Jefferies Hydro 4 p.m.–midnight; Monday November 9 Jefferies midnight–10 p.m. St. Stephen Hydro not scheduled to run on either date. Operator's November 7 daily facility discharge table lists Jefferies Hydro 4,004, St. Stephen Hydro 0, Spillway Hydro 7 and Spilling 770 (units not independently reconciled in this audit); November 6 lists Jefferies 4,192 and St. Stephen 0. These are reported facility entries, NOT direct Diversion Canal flow measurements. The tentative schedule does not establish actual generation or canal discharge.

INTERPRETATION — CONDITIONAL INFERENCE, NOT MEASURED FLOW: If the two reported lake elevations share a comparable vertical reference and describe the same general period, Marion standing nominally above Moultrie is consistent with potential Marion-to-Moultrie movement. The shrinking nominal difference may indicate reduced driving head, but cannot establish current direction at a specific canal location, strength, velocity or whether flow has changed. Santee Cooper explains that changing Moultrie storage and St. Stephen output can affect the lake-to-lake head and diversion flows, but this is operating context, not a current canal-flow observation. Classification: canal current NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED; no strength estimate is defensible.

SOURCES CHECKED NOVEMBER 8, 2026: Santee Cooper official operational feed (updated November 8; elevations/discharges dated November 7; tentative November 8–9 schedule): https://azapp-lakespublic-prd-001.azurewebsites.net/ ; Santee Cooper lake-data FAQ on Diversion Canal and hydraulic head: https://www.santeecooper.com/community/lakes/lake-data/ ; USGS Marion at Elloree https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02169921/ and Moultrie at Pinopolis https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172000/ (HTTP 403; independent readings and vertical datum reconciliation unavailable). Replaces November 7 commentary.
level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
